title: Restriction transport at a geometric point: coefficient normalization and derived naturality
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Let $g:s\to s$ be any scheme automorphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], not necessarily one over $k_0$. Use the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and inverse image $G=g^{-1}$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. For $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ or $\mathcal O_E$, use the finite constant or completed coefficient sheaf $\Lambda_s$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and the structure isomorphism $c_\Lambda:G\Lambda_s\to\Lambda_s$ [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. The action on $GM$ is transported by $c_\Lambda^{-1}$.

Write $U=(s\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}s)$ and $V=(s\xrightarrow g s)$. For a sheaf $M$ of $\Lambda_s$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], let $\operatorname{ins}_{g,M}:M(V)\to(GM)(U)$ be the coprojection at $(V,(\mathrm{id},\mathrm{id}):U\to u_g(V))$ into the inverse-image colimit of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], followed by sheafification. Define $\sigma^g_M=\operatorname{ins}_{g,M}\operatorname{res}_g:M(U)\to(GM)(U)$. Under the natural evaluation identification $(GM)(U)\cong M(V)$ of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image], $\operatorname{ins}_{g,M}$ is the identity, so $\sigma^g_M$ identifies with restriction along $g:V\to U$. For a constant section $b\in\Lambda$ one has $\sigma^g_{\Lambda_s}(b)=c_\Lambda^{-1}(b)$, and $\sigma^g_M(bx)=c_\Lambda^{-1}(b)\sigma^g_M(x)$.

Termwise on any unbounded complex $N$, these maps form a $\Lambda$-linear chain map $\sigma^g_N:\Gamma(s,N)\to\Gamma(s,GN)$, natural in chain maps. Here both module actions use constant sections and the target uses $c_\Lambda^{-1}$. For every derived morphism $v:N\to N'$ in $D(s_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the induced maps satisfy $\Gamma(s,Gv)\sigma^g_N=\sigma^g_{N'}\Gamma(s,v)$; thus they define a natural transformation on the entire derived category. The sections functor is that of [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]; no constructibility, boundedness or derived-completeness hypothesis on $N$ is imposed.

proof.text: Use the canonical sectionwise inverse-image coordinates already supplied by [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image]. The raw map is restriction along the specified site arrow. Naturality of the constant-presheaf sheafification unit gives restriction of a constant section as the same constant section at the new object. The normalization clause of isoSectionwiseConstantMap_existsUnique then says that the specified finite coefficient comparison sends this restricted constant back to the original constant.

source.place: Tags 0H7J, 09A5 and 00WX; constant-section normalization in the recorded sectionwise model.

proof.text: For completed coefficients apply every finite projection. The limit.lift projection equations identify both the constant-to-completion map with its quotient leg and the completed coefficient comparison with inverse image of the projection followed by the finite comparison. Naturality of the projection moves it past restriction. Naturality of sheafification carries an integral constant to its quotient constant, so the finite normalization proves equality after each projection. Evaluation preserves the ring-sheaf limit and the forgetful functor from rings to sets preserves this limit, hence joint injectivity proves the completed identity. Applying the inverse coefficient comparison gives the first clause of the theorem.

proof.text: Restriction in a module presheaf is semilinear. Replace its restricted scalar by the inverse coefficient comparison using the first clause. This proves the second clause and gives a linear component for the specified source and target scalar restrictions. Presheaf naturality of a module morphism gives naturality of these components. The resulting natural transformation has exactly the raw restriction map as its underlying function.

source.place: Tag 06UM, restriction of module sections and naturality.

proof.text: Establish exact point sections in the independent coefficient universe required here. For an algebraically closed field the prime spectrum is a singleton and hence w-local; the field is strictly henselian, and its maximal localizations are itself. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-wcontractible-geometric-criterion] to get the required retractions of faithfully flat weakly etale field algebras. Then [lem-weil-pbc-wcontractible-affine-weakly-contractible] makes evaluation of epimorphisms of set sheaves surjective in the enlarged coefficient universe. Forgetting module operations carries an epimorphism to a locally surjective abelian-sheaf map and hence an epimorphism of set sheaves, so evaluation preserves epimorphisms of modules. Evaluation preserves kernels sectionwise and is additive; Mathlib exact-functor lemmas give preservation of finite limits and colimits. Scalar restriction is exact since its composite with the reflecting forgetful functor to abelian groups is the ordinary forgetful functor. Thus the specified scalar-valued sections functor is exact. The transported inverse image is exact by [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image].

source.place: Tags 0982 and 098H; the recorded affine ring-retraction evaluation theorem and geometric criterion.

proof.text: Apply mapHomologicalComplex to the module natural transformation and whisker with derived localization. Exactness supplies the two unbounded mapDerivedCategory functors and their canonical factorization isomorphisms. Apply Localization.liftNatTrans from [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. Its component equation, followed by cancellation of the target factorization isomorphism with its inverse, gives precisely the final displayed equation. Naturality is built into the lifted natural transformation, so it holds for every derived morphism.

tool_uses.why: Generic site-equivalence evaluation and finite coefficient structure isomorphism for any scheme isomorphism; the unit contains no substitute for these point-transport calculations.

lean.note: Uses the recorded canonical sectionwise inverse-image model: the distinguished coprojection is identity in its normalized evaluation coordinates. Option ℕ records the two allowed coefficient choices, some n meaning exponent n+1 and none meaning the completed integral sheaf. The derived functors and transformation are specified by their localization factorization and component formula, so no exactness, boundedness, constructibility, completeness or chosen derived map is an added hypothesis. Site and coefficient universes are independent.
